2027-01-08.alt: Season of Denha. The Third Qudasha is used today.
2027-01-08.verse: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.
theo: On the Fridays of Denha the Church honours the great witnesses who made Christ known. The first is John the Baptist, who saw the heavens open over Jesus at the Jordan. Isaiah had foretold his mission: a voice crying in the wilderness to prepare the way of the Lord, so that “the glory of the LORD shall be revealed, and all people shall see it together.” In the synagogue of Antioch in Pisidia St Paul tells the whole story of Israel, from Egypt to David, and then names the forerunner: “before his coming John had already proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.” And John himself said: “I am not he. No, but one is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of the sandals on his feet.”

John paid for his witness with his life. He told Herod plainly: “It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.” Herod feared him, “knowing that he was a righteous and holy man”, and even liked to listen to him; but at a birthday banquet, out of regard for his oaths and his guests, he sent a soldier to behead him in prison. Herod's power withered like grass; John's witness still speaks. “The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.” St Paul, himself “a prisoner for Christ Jesus”, shows what such witness builds: a household in which strangers become “citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone.” John, the last of the prophets, belongs to that foundation. The question he leaves us is simple: will I speak the truth with love, whatever it costs?

2027-01-08.prayer: O God, you sent John the Baptist to prepare the way of your Son and to bear witness to the truth even to death. Give us his humility, to point always to Christ, and his courage, to speak the truth with love; and build us with all your saints into a dwelling place for you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Third Qudasha is used today. At the altar we unite ourselves with John, the prophets and the apostles, the foundation on which the household of God is built.

family.explain: John the Baptist told King Herod that he was doing wrong. Herod put John in prison, even though he knew that John was a good and holy man. John was brave because he loved God and the truth.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard to tell the truth? How can we be brave?”

illus: Some years ago a young Syro-Malabar priest in a North Indian mission spoke out against a landlord who was cheating poor tribal labourers. He received threats and was transferred for his safety. Years later the labourers' children, now educated, invited him back as chief guest. They said: you were our John the Baptist.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, John the Baptist prepared your way and bore witness to the truth even to death. Give us his courage and his humility. Amen.
share: Prepare the way of the Lord (Isaiah 40:3). What in my life needs to be made straight for the Lord?
I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandals (Acts 13:25). Do I point to Christ or to myself?
It is not lawful for you (Mark 6:18). Where is God asking me to speak a hard truth with love?
interc: For the persecuted Church, especially in Asia and Africa.
For prophets in our time who speak the truth to the powerful.
For rulers, that they may listen to conscience.
For those who have been silenced, threatened or imprisoned.
For our group, that we may speak the truth with love.
pm.close: Lord God, John the Baptist gave his life for the truth. Strengthen us to witness to Christ without fear, and protect all who suffer for his name. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, on the Fridays of Denha the Church remembers the witnesses of Christ. Today we honour John the Baptist, who saw the heavens open at the Jordan. Long before, Isaiah had heard a voice crying: in the wilderness prepare the way of the Lord (Isaiah 40:3). John was that voice.

In Antioch St Paul tells the story of Israel, from Egypt to King David, and then says: before the coming of Jesus, John proclaimed a baptism of repentance to all the people. And John said: I am not he; one is coming after me, and I am not worthy to untie his sandals (Acts 13:24–25). The greatness of John is that he points away from himself.

John told Herod: it is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife (Mark 6:18). Herod knew that John was a righteous and holy man, and even liked to listen to him. But at his birthday banquet, to keep a rash oath and to save face before his guests, he had John beheaded in prison. Truth spoken with love can be costly.

Where is Herod's power now? The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever (Isaiah 40:8). St Paul, writing as a prisoner for Christ, tells us that we are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone (Ephesians 2:20). John's witness, sealed in blood, is part of that foundation.
Let us ask for John's humility, to point always to Christ, and for his courage, to speak the truth with love. And let us pray for Christians who today are imprisoned or killed for their faith. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was very brave. He told the king the truth even when it was dangerous. Let us always tell the truth, kindly and bravely.
